key_insight: Quantum models showed a clear accuracy advantage over classical baselines on MNIST, but they traded that gain for higher runtime.
engineering_relevance: For practical deployment, the study suggests quantum methods are most attractive when accuracy gains or resource efficiency justify added computational cost and quantum hardware complexity.
method: Benchmarked CSVM vs QSVM and CCNN vs QCNN on MNIST
Varied feature dimensionality, sample size, and execution environment (CPU/GPU)
Compared accuracy, runtime, parameter count, and memory requirements
evidence_signal: Across the evaluated settings, QSVM reached about 0.90 accuracy versus about 0.85 for CSVM at 1,000 samples, while QCNN and CCNN both exceeded 0.96 accuracy at 64 features and 60,000 samples.
watch_item: The reported quantum advantages come with higher runtime and depend on feature/sample scaling, so results may not transfer directly to larger real-world or hardware-constrained workloads.
paper_title: Do We Really Need Quantum Machine Learning?: A Multidimensional Empirical Study
